title: global liquidity / monetary policy transmission / international capital flows | Research Paper | The Shifting Drivers of Global Liquidity
summary: This Federal Reserve Bank of New York Staff Report (No. 819, June 2017, revised August 2019) examines how the sensitivity of global liquidity components—international loan and bond flows—to global factors varied over the post-crisis decade. The authors find that sensitivity to U.S. monetary policy rose substantially after the global financial crisis, peaked around the 2013 Fed 'taper tantrum,' and then reverted toward pre-crisis levels. Meanwhile, the responsiveness of international bank lending to global risk conditions declined steadily throughout the post-crisis period. The main driver of fluctuations in sensitivity to U.S. monetary policy was the degree of convergence among advanced economy monetary policies, while the post-crisis decline in bank lending sensitivity to risk was driven by increases in lending shares of better-capitalized banking systems.
